claim.statement: Φ (the substrate's reasoning-state phi value) is invariant to walk trajectory details when the underlying concept SET is held constant. M.57 observed phi delta = 0.0 EXACTLY across 15 word-shuffled prompts — even when walks differed by 11% in concept overlap. This refines the M.46 F3 reproducibility finding: Φ matches within 0.01 across fresh-Takwin instances on the same prompt, but matches EXACTLY across word-order perturbations on the same concept set. Φ is a set-function, not a trajectory-function.
claim.operationalization: Examine the Φ delta distribution across 15 word-shuffled prompt pairs. Confirm that walks differ (Jaccard < 1.0 on some prompts) WHILE Φ values are identical.
claim.h0: Φ varies with walk trajectory (delta > 0 even when concept set preserved)

preregistration.analysis_plan: Confirm Φ delta uniformly = 0 across word-shuffled prompts.

detail.interpretation: Φ is decoupled from walk trajectory under same-concept-set conditions
Φ is more invariant to word order than to fresh-Takwin re-initialization — Φ is mechanically determined by graph topology, not by stochastic factors

verdict.reasoning: All 15 prompt pairs had Φ delta = 0.0 to numerical precision. Walks differed (mean Jaccard 0.892, not 1.000) yet Φ matched exactly. This mechanically implies Φ depends on the GeoidGraph topology built from the concept set, not on the specific path the Walker took through that graph.
